column8: Tue 24 Nov: Store, claim 1's primary text for the cost-of-change curve (Q47 A10's Beach figures are second-hand, so this replaces them if one is cited); the plan's three dated purchases (January 2027, January 2028, the move before the 2031 meetings) are purchases, never proofs or drafts (V2.4 guard 3, card Q82); no report turn.

Tue 24 Nov: Team notes for 3c-3d only: a stated figure is dear to change because co-sponsors count the top ($115,000; funder test, voice round 17); 3d is plain, so never in her words; say co-sponsors count the top, never their target (SD-1 demoted).

Tue 24 Nov: Store, behind 3e's plain point that the plan removes the event rather than pricing it (nothing stated before it is owned, IPS l.15; NUMBERS 8u's breaks); never put a number on credibility; no slot in 3e, which holds the gilt crisis as its one outside parallel.

Tue 24 Nov: Fix the map before use: the top sits below what is owned ($117,142 stated $115,000, NUMBERS 3 and 4) because of the 0.5% and the rounding to the safe side (Q141-022), not to price a late change; 3b already holds Richmond and the IHO rule, so store only.

Tue 24 Nov: Store, the evidence under row 7: contracts charge the author only for changes after setting; the plan's twin is NUMBERS 8u's three verbs (a figure not yet stated is lowered and breaks nothing; only a stated one breaks); nothing about Laura's own contracts (guard 5).
Tue 24 Nov: Colour only, evidence for row 5 that the allowance is custom; no plan relation.

Tue 24 Nov: 3e, one plain clause: the plan's only cushions (the 0.5% margin, the room under the top of about 2% in all, the letter's C3) cover others' slips, and IPS l.17 leaves none for a change of mind; checked against NUMBERS 3, 4 and 8u. Fix: 3e already holds the gilt crisis as its outside parallel and erase every pencil line as its turn, so say it plainly without the contract frame; never call the 0.5% an allowance.

Tue 24 Nov: The plan's point is plain and dated (IPS l.17's two reasons written in the IPS of 7 Nov 2026, before the January 2027 purchase; the 30 Sep bar before any number was run); the code would be a second outside parallel in 3e, and 3f names no outside source (ARGUMENT_TREE), so the code stays in the store.

Tue 24 Nov: Store, behind 3e's plain line that once a figure is owned the plan changes only when it cannot be carried out (no deposit by 31 March 2028; a Treasury payment more than five business days late, NUMBERS 8u); the IPS's reasons are events, never corrections or errors in the plan (CANON A34).
Tue 24 Nov: Taiwan twin of row 9 from one editor's blog, English Keel's; client colour only; never Taiwan's funders expect this.
Tue 24 Nov: Colour only: about the illustration trade, no plan relation; never about Laura's own work (guard 5).

Tue 24 Nov: Her trade's pencil roughs move freely and finished art costs to change, the shape of NUMBERS 8u's lowered against breaks; fix: the trade's step is approval, which carries the signed-off sense the conceit keeps out (V2.2 3c: completed, never approved), and 2.0's one fact is Q141-026, so store; never her roughs (guard 5).

Tue 24 Nov: Team notes behind COSPONSOR_NOTES C3 only (the letter fixes $115,000 and any shortfall in what the fund pays comes from her flexibility, NUMBERS 4): the trades' rule that bringing delivery up to the brief costs the buyer nothing; 3d is plain, never in her words or as a turn.

Tue 24 Nov: Store, pedigree for 3e's decided method (one risk per sentence with who covers it, voice round 13; NUMBERS 8u's sets): whose fault decides who pays; a method fact, never a turn or a proof image.
Tue 24 Nov: Current evidence for row 1's curve and row 14's split; its useful edge (a printed fix is optional, a stated figure left short breaks) is NUMBERS 8u's already.
Tue 24 Nov: The manuals' wording for the stet entry Q82-035 already holds; store only, never pointed at the IPS (guard 3).

Tue 24 Nov: Writers' guard, store: stet undoes a wrong mark, so as a picture of holding it would say the team keeps reconsidering; the plan holds because a market fall is never marked (IPS l.17); claim 2 killed with Q82-035; whether BS 5261's tick is circled is unverified.

Tue 24 Nov: 3e and Table 3's prose, plain: each watch is read on its date and a check that finds none of the named events changes nothing (Q220: never automatic or stop-loss; IPS l.17); the blank-margin rule is the fact behind it, never a proofreading image, since the page being proofed would make the plan a proof (guard 3).

Tue 24 Nov: Store only: the copout has stet's shape (a proposed strike withdrawn against the 30 Sep bar), but 3f is plain with its one turn and names no outside source, and stet is never pointed at the IPS or Trading Notes (guard 3); Q46 not re-read.
Tue 24 Nov: Colour only; the PRC standard's keep mark maps nothing, claim 2 being killed.
Tue 24 Nov: Writers' accuracy guard only: BS 5261 uses a symbol, Chicago writes stet; moot while stet stays out of the report.

Tue 24 Nov: A literal pencil-and-ink rule from proofreading, but its pencil means not sure, the deliberative sense the conceit avoids (Q114-036; the top is decided by IPS l.15 and pencil only until owned), and 2.0's one fact is Q141-026; store, a fallback if NP100's current wording fails; the Chinese rules are the PRC's, English Keel's.

Tue 24 Nov: Twin of Q82-027 (owning both ends does not end the watching): after the move Table 3 checks presence and timing (the late-2032 fund held, the notice watch in September-October, each payment within five business days); never final proof or sign-off for the move (guard 3).

Tue 24 Nov: Store for Table 3 and 3e: each dated test fixes in advance what no news means (no deposit by 31 March 2028 is the first reason; a Treasury payment more than five business days late the second, NUMBERS 8u); print's default runs the other way, so plain words only.

Tue 24 Nov: 3c fallback behind inked before the 2031 meetings (IPS l.15 fixes the move; no figure is stated before it, NUMBERS 4), but third in line after Q141-027 and Q106-026 (one of the two at most), and a 000 lives in proofs, so it risks reading the range as a draft (card Q82, guard 3); the report prints today's reading, which a 000 never does; store.
Tue 24 Nov: Store behind row 25: the move's purchase-day spread falls outside both ends and the 0.5% (NUMBERS 0, money put in, checked); weak alone.

Tue 24 Nov: 3c fallback for why nothing is stated before the move; fix the source: 2.9%, 6.2%, 8.6% and 10.6% are NUMBERS 4's Why nothing is stated before the move, not 8u; outlines is a trade word a finance judge must decode (panel 3) and a second image for 3c's one verb; store.

Tue 24 Nov: Store: digital lettering goes on after inks, the order of Laura's rule (she states a figure only once it is inked, IPS l.15), while Q174-004 uses hand lettering's opposite order for the 2028 order of claims, so one of the two at most; never the words are fixed once inked (row 29).

Tue 24 Nov: 3e: the plain point that a liquid portfolio is held still by IPS l.17, not by price, answers a judge's why-not-trade; fix the figure: card Q45 gives the funds 0.04%-0.05% and small Treasury trades 0.07% on average, but her off-the-run bonds about 0.18%-0.40% round trip, so say under half a percent, never a few hundredths; the comics fact stays in the store (3e holds the gilt crisis).
Tue 24 Nov: Second leg of row 29 (the rule outlived the cost because the knock-on did not get cheaper), and the knock-on is row 2's co-sponsors count the top; a blogger and two presses' guides.

Tue 24 Nov: 2.2, the mechanism behind the order of purchase (IPS l.11-15): a surprise is absorbed by the lines after it, as the 2028 first slice ($39,162 at today's rates, NUMBERS 4) leaves less for the floor and VT, and nothing runs back into the ten; fix: Q79-036 and Q174-002 already hold the order, so one parallel at most, and never overrun (the IPS's word for building costs, card Q82).

Tue 24 Nov: Refuse: its only map makes her flexibility a galley, a draft of a page, against IPS l.15 (promised to no one) and Q47's misleading list (bleed for her flexibility); the plain point (its uses are not yet known) is 3b's already.
Tue 24 Nov: Twin of row 8 (settled before the work starts), from the PRC's code with Keel's English; adds little.
Tue 24 Nov: Colour only, repeats the patched ink already in the store (Q44-009, Q44-010; V2.3).

Tue 24 Nov: Title page only, Caplet's call: the text exists in 法書要錄 卷一 and maps only the order (prepare, then write), not own then state, since a settled idea is pencil; Chinese only, traditionally attributed; supersedes Q47 A18's wording; Q121-032 (Chen Uen) is the Taiwanese alternative.
Tue 24 Nov: Title page: the text reads 意在筆前 (MOE headword), 意在筆先 being a later form; already carried into CONCEIT V2.2 tonight, and it saves an error a Chinese-reading judge would catch.
Tue 24 Nov: Citation fix for Q47 A18 (王俊鈞, 東海中文學報 36, 2018, pp. 69-100); the article is not in WORKS_CITED_DRAFT, so it matters only if cited; the lead edits.
Tue 24 Nov: Title page wording: say traditionally attributed to Wang Xizhi; Usami read only through 王俊鈞, so cite 王俊鈞 if anything.

Tue 24 Nov: Title page wording, with a date: the doubt goes back to Sun Guoting in 687 (his words name the 筆陣圖, not the afterword); the map to we modelled is a writing rule, not a plan relation, so one clause in the store at most.
Tue 24 Nov: English back-up for the doubted attribution, secondary and hedged both ways; References only if an English source is needed.

Tue 24 Nov: Title page guard, now in CONCEIT V2.2: the one English translation read at source says pretending to grind the ink (Shi 2017, after Gao), so any English is Shi's with the translator named, never grind the ink before you write; Gao 2012 unread.
Tue 24 Nov: Evidence for row 7's guard: three readings of 先乾研墨, two from web essays, so no English line rests on grind.

Tue 24 Nov: Refuse: its map needs Lady Wei's idea to stand for money owned, which the card's own claim 1 calls pencil; its battle words make the first plan's end a defeat, against CANON A3 (dropped for IPS l.9's reason); and 3f is plain with one turn and no outside source; Barnhart read via Shi.

Tue 24 Nov: 3b, a strikingly dissimilar fact for the split IPS l.15 and l.17 draw: the ten and both stated ends set in advance, her flexibility the one place she decides as things change; fix: idea first is a decision, not ink (the top is decided by IPS l.15 and pencil until owned), so it maps set against open, never owned; it does not sit behind ink only goes one way, so a second image in 3b: store or a reader test; Shi's English.

Tue 24 Nov: Store: forecasts drift on the day as Zheng's bamboo did, while what Treasuries pay does not; 3e holds its one turn and the gilt crisis, so a second image there; Zheng praises the drift; a long quote in Keel's English.
Tue 24 Nov: Title page provenance only: if an epigraph is used, a copy of the line is in Taipei (NPM 故書000398); no plan relation; Huang's text reads 乾硯墨.

Tue 24 Nov: Title page, Caplet's call: Sun Guoting's 意先筆後 (687, scroll in Taipei) avoids the doubted attribution and maps only the order; fix: read the passage around the phrase in full before use (the card's gap), since beside 瀟灑流落 it may describe a master's ease, not preparation.
Tue 24 Nov: Colour only, never a turn: armour can be pierced and protects without owning, pulling away from ink as owned (UCC 8-503); a war image beside an arts residency.

Tue 24 Nov: The Close, answering IPS l.19 (you take risks on the page): strokes alike like counting rods are not calligraphy, while ten identical $50,000 payments, each maturing just before its date (IPS l.13), are the point; fix: say payments, never identical rungs (five iBond funds, five T-bonds, NUMBERS 0); 3a holds its turn and the lottery, so the Close or a reader test; never at her art; doubted text, Keel's gloss.
Tue 24 Nov: Refuse: colour only, and its one tempting map (the heirs line beside the letter's estate clause) would carry the conceit into 3d, which is plain.
Tue 24 Nov: Client colour only: Taiwanese readers meet this text through 一波三折; an idiom is not evidence for building-cost twists, never in Laura's words.
Tue 24 Nov: Client knowledge for the epigraph only: Taiwan's dictionary names Wang plainly, so traditionally attributed sits beside it; that a Taiwanese reader will not resent it is Keel's guess.
Tue 24 Nov: Kills claim 3's slow grinding (the Smithsonian wants a stone that grinds quickly); a guard, no plan relation.

Tue 24 Nov: Twin of row 22 (preparation sized to the work); its wording garbles the plan: the 2027 deposit bought the ten, and the 2028 first slice ($39,162) completes them and buys the extra Treasuries (NUMBERS 4).
Tue 24 Nov: Store, kills claim 3's could not be skipped; never in 3f, which is plain with its one turn.

Tue 24 Nov: 3c, behind two inkings, two dates: the top's size is set by how much moves at the January 2031 move, before the meetings (NUMBERS 4), as ink's strength is set at the stone; fix: third in line after Q141-027 and Q106-026, one at most; a calligrapher can grind more mid-work, while a stated range is never raised (Q154).

Tue 24 Nov: 3a, behind never an endowment (WORDS): the ten Treasuries exist to be spent, one maturing before each payment to January 2042; fix: 3a holds its turn and the lottery, so a second image; Su Shi's point is vanity and mortality, never imply Laura hoards; one of rows 24 and 26.
Tue 24 Nov: Store only: a supply sized in years like the ten; the line is about ageing and the plan's length is the case's, so a weak map.
Tue 24 Nov: The Taipei twin of row 24 (an ink cake that survives because it was never ground), one of the two at most; colour risk, since museum objects exist to survive.

Tue 24 Nov: Store: payments as consumables and the building as the lasting thing; weak, since the building's money is paid once, in January 2033, and is not lasting money in the plan.
Tue 24 Nov: Client knowledge only: Taiwan's registered inkstone craft and its dated yearly plan; the rhythm map to the ten yearly payments is weak, and a co-sponsor's rhythm is Keel's guess.
Tue 24 Nov: Process guard: an official page's origin story has no document behind it, so never the bridge story; the 1916 report seen only through 林文龍.
